title: Gowers norm and the low-degree test acceptance probability
statement:
Fix $n$ and an integer $d \ge 0$, and let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ be a Boolean-valued function with $\pm1$ lift $(-1)^f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{\pm1\}$. Then the probability that the $(d+1)$-fold derivative low-degree test accepts $f$ is
\[
  \Pr[\text{accept}] \;=\; \frac{1 + \|(-1)^f\|_{U^{d+1}}^{2^{d+1}}}{2},
\]
where $\|(-1)^f\|_{U^{d+1}}^{2^{d+1}}$ is the $(d+1)$-st Gowers uniformity norm of the lift raised to the power $2^{d+1}$.
hypotheses_covered: an order parameter d : ℕ (giving a (d+1)-fold test)
